item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development to implement a feature unit that adds retry behavior to a failing operation.
special_constraints: Do not write production code before red proof.
success_definition: Uses red-green-refactor ordering.
Writes or identifies a failing test before implementation.
Verifies the red failure for the expected reason.
Keeps the green implementation minimal.
Reports red, green, and refactor evidence.
Optionally includes a condensed sanitized output summary when command output helps review.

item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development for a bug where a stale cache entry remains after account deletion.
special_constraints: Bug fix needs a red signal or executable reproducer before the fix.
success_definition: Creates or isolates a failing test or reproducer.
Confirms the failure proves the causal hypothesis.
Implements only the minimal fix.
Reruns the target proof green and then broader relevant checks.

item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development after noticing implementation code was already written before any failing test for the current unit.
special_constraints: Discard only agent-authored implementation hunks for this unit.
Do not use destructive git commands.
success_definition: Stops implementation-first flow.
Identifies that the current unit must restart from RED.
Protects pre-existing and user-authored changes.
Avoids broad reset or checkout commands.
Reports the restart and then follows red-green-refactor.

item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development on a pure configuration metadata rename with no behavior-bearing code path.
special_constraints: A TDD exception may be valid, but it must be explicit.
success_definition: Recognizes the change as a potential TDD exception.
States why TDD is not warranted.
Names the alternate verification path.
Does not silently skip validation.

item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development for a feature with three desired behaviors. The plan currently lists all three tests before any implementation work.
special_constraints: Use tracer bullets: one behavior test, one minimal implementation, then repeat.
Prefer public-interface or real-chain tests and avoid mocks of internal collaborators.
success_definition: Identifies all-tests-first/all-code-second as horizontal slicing.
Chooses one observable behavior as the first tracer bullet.
Requires RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR for that behavior before starting the next behavior.
Keeps tests focused on public interfaces or real chains where practical.
Avoids speculative implementation for future tests.

item.arguments: Use $fw:test-driven-development for a feature where the user listed five possible behaviors and only two are critical for the first slice.
special_constraints: Keep a behavior/test list prioritized by value and risk.
Choose the next highest-value observable behavior instead of trying to cover everything.
Use the smallest credible implementation, then generalize only when more executable test cases or reproducers require it.
Refactor after green to remove duplication or improve the public interface.
success_definition: Creates or carries a prioritized behavior/test list.
Chooses one next behavior to drive the current cycle.
Keeps the implementation minimal for that behavior without speculative generalization.
Uses additional executable test cases or reproducers to justify generalization rather than guessing.
Refactors only after green and focuses refactoring on duplication, clarity, or interface quality.
